deep.reconstruction: Folio 2r carries no legible original writing of its own. The only clear mark is the pencilled folio number '2' in the right margin, probably an archivist's foliation. The faint grey formulas in the upper right quadrant read mirror-reversed: the letters and the '+' and '=' signs are backwards. That pattern indicates show-through (or offset) from writing on the reverse of the leaf or a facing sheet, not text written on this side. The ghost layout matches the previous page: a fraction with a long fraction bar near the top, a line of the form '... = ... + ...', and short lines below. That page dealt with linear fractional (Möbius) maps. Its content, restated here for context only, ran as follows. Riemann takes the map z -> (az+b)/(cz+d) and seeks gamma such that gamma*z+1 is carried to a constant multiple of itself. Writing gamma*(az+b)/(cz+d) + 1 = (gamma*(az+b)+cz+d)/(cz+d) and requiring gamma*(az+b)+cz+d = (b*gamma+d)(gamma*z+1), the constant terms agree identically. The z-coefficients give gamma*a + c = gamma*(b*gamma+d), i.e. a + c/gamma = b*gamma + d. Equivalently b*gamma^2 + (d-a)*gamma - c = 0, whose roots gamma1 and gamma2 correspond to the two fixed points z = -1/gamma_i. With the new variable Z = (gamma1*z+1)/(gamma2*z+1), the map becomes Z -> [(b*gamma1+d)/(b*gamma2+d)] Z. This is the multiplier normal form of a loxodromic or hyperbolic Möbius transformation. The earlier line 'Z -> (rho^2/rho1^2) Z' ties this to repeated inversions (image charges) in two circles, i.e. the electrostatics of two parallel cylinders, the subject of the bundle 'ElektrCyl'. Nothing on 2r itself can be read beyond these ghost images, so no derivation can be attributed to this page.
